dateline: New Delhi / Islamabad / Gilgit-Baltistan / Srinagar / United Nations — August 1947–Present
heroHeadline: Ceasefire Holds at Day 501 as Salamabad Cross-LoC Trade Post Closes for Good, Operation Sohan Search Widens to Five Districts, and MEA Presses Pakistan on Afghanistan Strikes
heroSubtitle: September 23, 2026: Jammu & Kashmir formally handed the Salamabad Trade Facilitation Centre at Uri — one of two official cross-LoC trade points opened in 2008 — to the Tourism Department under a September 12 order, closing the chapter on a route that had already sat frozen since India suspended cross-LoC trade in April 2019; PDP president Mehbooba Mufti objected September 20, urging Chief Minister Omar Abdullah to seek its restoration from New Delhi. In Jammu region, the search for a third, reportedly injured Jaish-e-Mohammed militant from the September 16-17 Operation Sohan encounter near Udhampur — which killed two Pakistan-based terrorists — widened September 20 into a high alert across five districts (Kathua, Samba, Udhampur, Doda, Kishtwar), with drones, sniffer dogs and thermal-equipped helicopters deployed; no further casualties reported. Separately, India's MEA on September 22 condemned Pakistani airstrikes on Afghanistan's Kunar and Paktika provinces that killed at least three civilians, spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal pairing condolences with a pointed message that Islamabad 'must take credible action against cross-border terrorism before the world believes what they say they are going to do.' Across the Line of Control itself, no firing or infiltration incidents have been recorded since the August 27-29 drone cluster, and the ceasefire holds at Day 501 with no confirmed cross-border fire exchange since May 10, 2025. In Pakistan-administered Kashmir, the internet and mobile-data blackout imposed June 5 amid the JKJAAC-led unrest remains in force past 100 days, per NetBlocks, with JKHRO's verified death toll for the unrest still standing at 89 as of the sources reviewed. Bilateral freeze remains otherwise comprehensive: no ambassadors, $0 formal trade, IWT in abeyance despite the August 31 Hague arbitration ruling against India's suspension of the treaty.
footerNote: Data sourced from Indian MEA/MOD, Pakistan ISPR/MFA, UN Security Council, SIPRI, Crisis Group, HRW, Stimson Center
